title: The Letter of Hatib
subtitle: The Intercepted Missive at Rawdat Khakh, the Divine Vindication of Badr, and Surah Al-Mumtahanah
summary: As secret preparations commenced in Madinah for the march on Makkah, Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah—a decorated veteran of Badr—attempted to dispatch a covert warning to Quraysh through a female courier to protect his vulnerable kin. Intercepted through divine revelation at Rawdat Khakh by Ali, Al-Zubayr, and Al-Miqdad, the episode culminated in a profound manifestation of prophetic forbearance, the immortal defense of the veterans of Badr, and the revelation of Surah Al-Mumtahanah.

sections.text: Strict Confidentiality and the Secret Mobilization

Following the tragic breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah at Al-Watir, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved to liberate Makkah from polytheism and restore the sacred sanctuary to pure monotheistic worship. To avert bloodshed within the holy precinct and secure a peaceful surrender, the Prophet enforced an unprecedented level of operational secrecy. He supplicated to Allah: 'O Allah, seize the eyes and ears of Quraysh so that we may come upon them suddenly in their land.' Orders were issued to mobilize without disclosing the intended destination, keeping even the closest companions unaware of whether the army would march north toward the Levant, east into the desert, or south toward Makkah.

In this atmosphere of tense anticipation, a human lapse occurred within the inner circle of the believers. Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, a courageous Muhajir who had fought valiantly at Badr and Uhud, was overcome by anxiety for his vulnerable family residing in Makkah. Unlike other emigrants who belonged to powerful clans capable of shielding their kin, Hatib was an ally (halif) without tribal protection. Hoping to secure a debt of goodwill from the chieftains of Quraysh, he drafted a brief letter warning them of the Prophet's impending movement and hired a traveler woman named Sarah to deliver it secretly, concealed within her hair braid.
Divine revelation immediately informed the Prophet of the breach. In an authentic narration recorded by Imam al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim, Ali ibn Abi Talib recalled the urgent mission:

بَعَثَنِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَا وَالزُّبَيْرَ وَالْمِقْدَادَ فَقَالَ: 'انْطَلِقُوا حَتَّى تَأْتُوا رَوْضَةَ خَاخٍ، فَإِنَّ بِهَا ظَعِينَةً مَعَهَا كِتَابٌ، فَخُذُوهُ مِنْهَا'
'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched myself, Al-Zubayr, and Al-Miqdad, saying: 'Go forth until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman on a camel carrying a letter; seize it from her!'' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3007, 4274; Sahih Muslim 2494)

The three riders galloped furiously for twelve miles until they intercepted the woman at Rawdat Khakh. They demanded the letter, but she vehemently denied carrying any document. When a search of her camel saddle yielded nothing, Al-Zubayr and Al-Miqdad hesitated, but Ali stood firm, declaring: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never lied, nor were we lied to! By Allah, you shall either produce the letter, or we shall uncover you!' Realizing their unyielding determination, the woman untied the braids of her hair and extracted the sealed parchment.
The Interrogation and the Forgiveness of Badr

The riders carried the letter directly back to Madinah. Opening the missive before the assembly, the Prophet read the inscription: 'From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the people of Makkah...' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Hatib and asked with measured restraint: 'What caused you to do this, O Hatib?'

Trembling with shame and remorse, Hatib offered his honest confession: 'O Messenger of Allah, do not rush to judgment against me. By Allah, I believe in Allah and His Messenger; I have not apostatized nor changed my faith, nor have I preferred disbelief after Islam. But I was an adherent among Quraysh without a clan to protect my family, while the other Muhajirun have relatives there to guard their property. I wished to secure a favor with them so that they might protect my kin.'

Listening with divine wisdom, the Prophet declared: 'As for him, he has spoken the truth to you.' But Umar ibn al-Khattab, burning with righteous indignation, drew his sword and exclaimed: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me strike off the neck of this hypocrite! He has betrayed Allah, His Messenger, and the believers!'
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ immediately stayed Umar's hand and uttered words that would echo across generations as the supreme testament to divine grace:

إِنَّهُ قَدْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا، وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ اطَّلَعَ عَلَى مَنْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا فَقَالَ: 'اعْمَلُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ فَقَدْ غَفَرْتُ لَكُمْ'
'He witnessed Badr! And what do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have already forgiven you!'' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3007; Sahih Muslim 2494)

Tears streamed down Umar's cheeks as he lowered his sword and replied: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' In commentary upon this dramatic encounter, Allah revealed the opening verses of Surah Al-Mumtahanah:

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وَعَدُوَّكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ تُلْقُونَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِالْمَوَدَّةِ وَقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِمَا جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ الْحَقِّ
'O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth...' (Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:1)

The incident of Hatib demonstrated that human vulnerability could touch even the most sincere believers, while highlighting the sublime prophetic capacity to weigh past righteousness against transient error. With the breach secured and the army purified of suspicion, the march toward Makkah commenced under the protective guidance of divine destiny.
